title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-queueing-util-reporting-fix
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Fixes burst-accounting bug that could cause over-throttling during sustained queueing; improves throughput guarantees and adds additional utilization metrics for Dedicated fleets.
description:
Context: Dedicated fleet autoscaler uses a token-bucket style burst allowance to temporarily raise throughput. We observed a customer case (SUP-1291) where sustained request queueing caused burst tokens to be double-counted during an internal resync path, resulting in oscillating throttles and degraded throughput.

This PR fixes the burst-accounting logic, tightens the throughput guarantee under queueing, and adds utilization reporting so SRE and product can track burst consumption over time.

Changes included (high level):
- Fix atomic handling of burst token refills during QueueDrain/Resync path to prevent double-crediting.
- Add a new metric dedicated.autoscaler.burst_tokens_consumed and expose burst_tokens_available for per-fleet dashboards.
- Add a queueing-aware throughput adjustment: when queue length > threshold, autoscaler reduces opportunistic burst dispatch to prioritize steady throughput guarantees.
- Add integration test that simulates sustained queueing and asserts no over-crediting and stable throughput.
- Minor refactor of tokenbucket.go to separate accounting vs dispatch logic (keeps external behaviour identical aside from bugfix).

Why this is important: Under heavy queueing, previous behaviour could temporarily inflate calculated available capacity leading to downstream thrashing and SLA blips. This change ensures Dedicated customers retain their contractual throughput guarantees while still allowing short bursts when safe.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduced issue in unit/integration test harness (simulated multi-node queueing).
- [x] Added regression test covering resync path double-crediting.
- [x] Updated observability (metrics and per-route dashboard queries).
- [x] Performance sanity check (latency / p50/p95 unaffected for steady-state workloads).
- [x] Run full CI and manual canary on a small dedicated pool.

Related: ENG-8421 implements the autoscaler rewrite where tokenbucket moved into the fleet controller. This PR is a targeted bugfix that lives in that codepath. SUP-1291 is the customer report that triggered investigation.

review_comments: Evan Hughes: Can you add a short comment explaining why we prefer reduction of opportunistic bursts when queueing is high? I want to make the reasoning explicit for future maintainers.

Asha Patel: Added fleet_id tag to metrics and updated dashboard JSON. Metrics instrumentation tests updated.
Ravi Menon: Integration test looks solid, but I saw one flaky run locally due to timing; increased allowances and added deterministic waits. Re-ran CI and it's stable.

summary: Fix autoscaler burst-accounting double-crediting during resync/queueing, add utilization metrics, and prevent over-throttling under sustained queueing.
notes_for_release: Critical bugfix for Dedicated autoscaler. Customers on Dedicated fleets may see improved throughput stability under high queueing after rollout. No config changes required; metrics exposed for observability.
